body:
**Authorized/Ready; unstarted pending the justified capacity rule.** The owner explicitly authorized the dependent compiler and proof changes once the rule is justified, recorded on main through [PR #120](https://github.com/berkeleynerd/silver/pull/120), merge `b5667af6a991fce7da1c13e3edc0b874d0d4adbc`, following the [retained-tool direction](https://github.com/berkeleynerd/silver/blob/main/docs/session-memory.md#2026-10-17--retained-tool-capacity-direction-adopted). #119 is the active prerequisite. No further implementation go-ahead is required within this scope; respect the recorded dependency order and claim each package before starting it. It depends on #87 and coordinates the representation/reporting distinction with #119 and #91. The [scope](https://github.com/berkeleynerd/silver/blob/main/docs/unbounded-programs.md#design) and [roadmap](https://github.com/berkeleynerd/silver/blob/main/roadmap.md#unbounded-programs) govern it; #97, #98, #100–#102 record the relevant review findings.

**Order 2.** Separate admission/build from per-program confirmation while preserving same-source identity and the strongest conditional assurance claims. Compilation publishes an admitted, successfully built program. Confirmation checks the concrete tool output and preserves the executable and recorded build result; detecting a defect does not certify that executable's semantic validity. This is not a promise that every unsuccessful tool invocation was caused by resource exhaustion.

**Commands and identity**

- `silver compile` admits, builds, prints the executable path and then confirms unless `--no-confirm` is given. Its build result and the later confirmation result are reported separately; a completed build remains successful if confirmation is inconclusive or finds a defect.
- `silver run` admits, builds and executes without confirming. It forwards the application's status as specified below.
- `silver confirm WORKSPACE` confirms the recorded `main.adb`, selected runtime snapshots and project inputs of a retained build workspace. Persist a build-input identity record and compare the inputs against it before any admission recheck and after confirmation. A missing/mismatched record or modified snapshot is an identity defect (3), including when the modified source is no longer a member; it is not a fresh membership rejection (2). The contract assumes a stable private workspace during each identity check/tool operation; do not describe this as executable attestation or as protection against adversarial concurrent replacement.
- Confirmation has no configured time limit. Explicit interruption cancels it and reports "not confirmed", retaining the build and executable. Print the paths and available sizes of retained `program-*` and `imagews-*` workspaces after an unsuccessful confirmation; failure to collect diagnostics must not overwrite the primary outcome.
- Replace the `Publish` ghost contract: publication follows admission, successful build and identity checks. A "confirmed" result requires the complete successful-report audit.

**Selected obligations.** Preserve the current source-selected `-U` policy. Output programs select Main and the six identity-bound runtime source files, and successful confirmation audits the Main report plus the four library-unit reports. Null programs retain the current exact Main-only selection and audit. Do not silently broaden or weaken either policy.

**Prover configuration**

- Keep `-U --mode=all --report=all --checks-as-errors=on --no-loop-unrolling` and the mode's `--warnings`; drop `--level`.
- Use `--prover=cvc5,z3,altergo --timeout=0 --memlimit=0 --steps=0 --counterexamples=off -j<max(3, CPUs)>`. Never set a finite `--steps` above 5,368,146. Preserve the pinned GNATprove 16.1 behavior: prover alternatives race, and a successful alternative may interrupt losing attempts.
- Validate actual prover invocations, not the synthetic memory field in a trivial-proof report, when checking that no prover memory limit remains. Record scheduler and tool identities and the distinction between configured limits and physical exhaustion.
- Re-execute the driver at most once with `RLIMIT_STACK` raised to the hard limit, with explicit failure handling; GNATprove, GPRbuild and the Image adapter inherit it. Linux confirmation children may request `oom_score_adj=1000`; this affects selection preference, does not guarantee a victim or prove an OOM cause, and an unavailable/failed adjustment is recorded.

**Outcome classifier.** Implement the decision procedure before relying on it in the CLI. Collect process completion/interruption and available reports, preserving leaf-level evidence. `--checks-as-errors=on` can give an ordinary nonzero exit after reports are finalized; "normal completion" does not mean exit zero.

**Representation versus observation.** #119/#91 must cover any finite representation needed for complete, faithful generation or translation of required obligations, or their automatic discharge. Its overflow on an admitted program is a defect (3), distinct from physical resource exhaustion; optional confirmation cannot waive it. A named boundary is eligible for confirmation-only treatment only when source/phase evidence establishes that it affects solely observation or reporting after the required proof work and cannot prevent or alter that work, and a reliable detection path distinguishes it from defects. Unknown coupling is unresolved, not a confirmation-only exception. Missing reports never establish successful confirmation.

- *Confirmed*: the selected run completed normally, all required reports pass the existing strict success policy and identity/coverage checks, and every required check is proved. A resource result or interrupted losing attempt does not poison a check already proved by another attempt.
- *Inconclusive*: no independent defect is established, and confirmation cannot be established because of an explicitly observed resource cause, an independently justified observation-only boundary as defined above, or explicit interruption. An unproved check is resource-inconclusive only when all its relevant unsuccessful attempts have attributable resource outcomes; a competing `Unknown`, `Invalid` or unexplained crash remains a defect candidate.
- *Defect*: definite non-proof with adequate resource evidence, an unproved check with an `Unknown`/`Invalid` or unexplained failure, missing proving coverage after normal completion without an independently established observation-only explanation, a normally completed report that violates required structure or policy, or a source-identity mismatch. Reaching a representation limit required for obligation generation or automatic discharge on admitted source is also a defect. An unexpectedly binding Silver-configured cap is a configuration defect even if the tool labels it `Timeout`, `StepLimitExceeded` or a memory-limit result. Unknown or conflicting causes map to defect/status 3, not a guessed resource failure.
- Keep the strict successful-report audit unchanged for claiming confirmation. Add a separate structural/identity/coverage inspection path for unsuccessful reports, so resource results are not rejected merely for failing the success predicate. Interruption, a known resource failure or an eligible observation-only boundary may leave missing/truncated reports; that expected incompleteness alone is not an independent defect. A defect established independently of the interruption/resource event retains precedence.
- Use `unproved_status` and per-prover `check_tree` evidence with their actual producer schema. A `High failure`/`signaled` report does not preserve a trustworthy numeric signal or resource cause. A shell exit 137, a child `SIGKILL`, or an increase in system-wide `/proc/vmstat` `oom_kill` is insufficient attribution. Retain these as diagnostics. Resource attribution requires a specific recognized tool result, captured errno, an attributable supervisor event, or equivalently direct evidence concerning this process/attempt.
- Write diagnostic bundles best effort for every unconfirmed result: source and identity record, available reports, tool identities, commands, statuses and attribution evidence. Defect bundles support bug reports. Bundle writing may itself fail through full disk, permissions or resource exhaustion; preserve the original classification and report the diagnostic failure.

**Exit statuses and observation boundaries**

- 0: successful `check`/catalogue export, successful build from `compile`, or confirmed `confirm`. A successful build's optional confirmation result is printed independently.
- 2: membership rejection or usage error. A failed read, allocation, write, launch or build is never a membership rejection.
- 3: compiler/confirmation defect, unexplained tool failure or unclassified environmental failure.
- 4: attributable compiler resource exhaustion, or standalone confirmation inconclusive through attributable resources, a recorded observation-only boundary satisfying the dependency test above, or explicit interruption.
- `run` forwards an ordinarily exited application's status, including 1, 2, 3, 4 or 137; those numbers do not classify its cause. Document the native signal-to-exit translation used by the implementation. A failed launch is a Silver outcome; in particular, captured launch `E2BIG` is status 4. Do not infer `Storage_Error` from application exit 1 or infer a signal from an ordinary exit 137.
- The driver's own fatal signal may prevent any Silver status being emitted. Either add a justified supervisor with attributable observations, or document the native environmental termination; never claim a universal conversion to 4.

Capture relevant failures across admission/storage, snapshot and identity I/O, workspace creation, Alire/project preparation and launch, GNAT frontend/gnatwhy3, GPRbuild/binder/linker, Image, Why3/provers, producer report writing and report reading/auditing. Define positive resource errno/tool cases separately from permission errors, missing tools/files, unsupported formats and tool crashes. Decode wait statuses at the process boundary; avoid inferring signals through shell/alr status collisions. Add top-level `Storage_Error` handling in `silver.adb` and `silver_image_adapter.adb` where it can run. Document each new libc binding and its trust obligation.

**Remove the command cap.** Replace fixed command construction/argument storage (including the 16,384-byte `Command_Buffer_Size` family) with growable storage and an argument-vector process interface. This package owns command construction and launch/status observation. #89 owns shared file/path/snapshot storage, ghost models and source certificates; agree the shared interface before either changes it. OS launch limits remain observable environmental failures, not a replacement Silver admission or command-length limit.

**Assurance and records.** Update `AGENTS.md`, `development.md`, `language.md`, README, catalogue as applicable, `docs/assurance.md` and `docs/trusted-boundary.md`, including every quoted command. Preserve all required obligations and same-source checks. State separately the universal solver-completion premise over admitted programs given sufficient resources, frontend acceptance, producer correctness/completeness, Image correctness and resource-outcome attribution. Confirmation checks concrete manifestations of those premises and does not establish them; moving it after build changes where failures are detected. Record stable-workspace and new process/errno bindings without inventing executable attestation.

**Lean.** Add a build-only pipeline (parse, fixed-library evidence, build) whose preservation and realization theorems do not use proof completion. Keep `automatic_pipeline` and `admitted_assurance` proving that every member's generated checks are discharged under `boundedProofCompletes`. Do not replace those stronger theorems by the build-only statement, add axioms, or claim Lean proves physical solver termination over the enlarged family.

**Completion criteria**

- Changed Silver-owned code has complete Bronze and Silver evidence; focused Lean targets have fresh axiom audits allowing only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
- Focused fixtures cover normal success, resource-only unsuccessful reports, `Unknown` mixed with resources, a proved check with a losing interrupted attempt, normal-completion missing coverage/malformed reports, interrupted partial reports, prior independent defect plus interruption, source mismatch and unknown signals. Distinguish proof-essential representation overflow (defect), a justified observation-only boundary (inconclusive), and an unidentified boundary (defect pending diagnosis). Test all observable phase/errno/status paths, best-effort bundles, ordinary application statuses and launch `E2BIG`. #94 integrates the full matrix; use bounded injections instead of giant resource-consuming runs where they test the same contract.
- Tests cover build without confirmation, retained-workspace confirmation identity, removal of the command cap, and unchanged source-selected successful audit policy. Update `tests/test_samples.py`, fixtures pinning proof options, and why3session limit expectations. Supported samples build/run/confirm with recorded expected outcomes.
- No claim relies on unavailable exit/signal/report information. The implementation, specification, documentation, catalogue and README agree; validation follows the repository's cost and iteration rules.
title: Unbounded programs: Proof confirmation and resource outcomes
